findings.description: `descending = sort.startswith("-")` treats any sort without a leading '-' as ascending. That is consistent with the documented API. However, in a URL query string a literal '+' prefix is decoded as a space, so `sort=+total` becomes ' total' and fails with a ValueError. Also, the default for orders_panel is descending=True but a plain `sort=total` from the query gives ascending, so behaviour differs between the two entry points. This is a minor contract inconsistency.
findings.suggestion: Strip whitespace and document that unprefixed means ascending, or keep the same default direction in both entry points.
findings.title: Sort prefix handling breaks the "-" direction and the "+" convention

findings.description: An explicitly empty `statuses` list returns no orders, but `panel_from_query` converts an empty or blank status parameter to None, which returns all orders. Direct callers passing `[]` get an empty result while the query path gets everything; this inconsistency may surprise callers. It is arguably intentional.
findings.suggestion: Document the semantics clearly or treat empty as no filter in both places.
findings.title: Empty status list is checked after unknown check but behaves differently from None
